extra.message: OS command injection via uploaded file content in Falcon FileUpload endpoint — Attacker-controlled uploaded file bytes are embedded into a shell command executed via os.system. [verified: user_input from uploaded file bytes is concatenated into cmd and passed to os.system with no sanitization, matching os.system(cmd) sink at line 29.]

OS command injection via uploaded file content — Remote attacker uploading a file can execute arbitrary shell commands on the server host [verified: Duplicate of finding 0; raw upload bytes reach os.system with no shell escaping.]

OS command injection via query parameter in Falcon ThreadView background thread — Attacker-controlled query parameter reaches os.system, enabling command execution. [verified: query param 'user_input' flows unsanitized through thread_function into os.system(cmd) at line 63-64, executed in background thread but still attacker-triggered.]

OS command injection via /thread query parameter — Unauthenticated remote attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands by supplying a crafted `user_input` query parameter to GET /thread [verified: Duplicate of finding 1; GET /thread query param 'user_input' reaches os.system unsanitized via thread_function.]

OS command injection via uploaded file bytes reaching os.system — Attacker uploading a crafted file can execute arbitrary shell commands on the server [verified: Uploaded file bytes (content[:20]) are passed directly to do_os_system, which calls os.system(command) with no validation, and file content is fully attacker-controlled.]

OS command injection in FastAPI /cmdi endpoint — Attacker-controlled query parameter user_input is concatenated into a shell command and executed via os.system, enabling RCE. [verified: user_input query param is concatenated unsanitized into a shell string and passed to os.system, no validation or escaping present.]

Command injection via uploaded file content — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server by uploading a file whose first 20 bytes contain a shell metacharacter payload [verified: apps/quart_app.py:23 reads raw uploaded file bytes and passes them to do_os_system, which calls os.system() unsanitized (src/vulnpy/trigger/cmdi.py:6) — no validation exists on this path.]

OS command injection via uploaded file bytes (Quart) — Attacker uploading a crafted file can execute arbitrary shell commands on the server [verified: Duplicate confirmation: same sink/flow as idx 0, only a ValueError catch surrounds it which does not sanitize or block shell metacharacters.]

OS command injection via os.system in cmdi trigger — Full shell command execution with attacker-controlled input, leading to remote code execution. [verified: do_os_system passes command directly to os.system with no sanitization, reachable from HTTP-facing trigger routes across all adapters.]

OS Command Injection via os.system — Arbitrary shell command execution on the host running the app. [verified: Same os.system sink as idx0, confirmed reachable via multiple framework routes with attacker-controlled header/query/form input.]

Insecure deserialization via pickle.load on user input — Arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payload supplied as user_input. [verified: pickle.load on attacker-controlled bytes with no sanitization or safe loader; deliberate RCE fixture.]

Code Injection via execfile on attacker-controlled path — Arbitrary Python code execution by pointing execfile at an attacker-writable/controlled file. [verified: do_execfile passes user_input straight into execfile() with no validation, allowing arbitrary code execution from an attacker-referenced file.]

SQL injection via string-formatted query in sqlite3 executescript trigger — Attacker input directly concatenated into multi-statement SQL script and executed. [verified: executescript allows multi-statement injection, increasing impact beyond single execute; input path identically unsanitized.]

Code injection via exec() on user-controlled input — Arbitrary Python code execution driven by HTTP request input. [verified: exec() runs raw user input directly with no sanitization on a reachable trigger path.]

Path traversal via unsanitized path passed to tarfile.TarFile.open — Arbitrary file access via attacker-supplied path/traversal sequences. [verified: tarfile.TarFile.open(user_input, mode="r:") uses the raw attacker-controlled string as the archive path with no checks.]

Path traversal via unsanitized file path passed to open() — Arbitrary local file read using attacker-controlled path traversal sequences. [verified: do_open/do_io_open/do_bz2_open/do_bz2_class/do_tarfile_* all pass user_input directly to filesystem open APIs with no path validation or sanitization anywhere in the file.]

SQL injection via string-formatted query in sqlite3 execute trigger — Attacker-controlled user_input is interpolated directly into an INSERT statement via str.format and executed, allowing arbitrary SQL injection (data exfiltration/modification). [verified: user_input flows unsanitized from HTTP route into str.format-built SQL string executed via cursor.execute, with no validation or parameterization.]

SQL injection via string-formatted query in sqlite3 executemany trigger — Attacker input directly concatenated into SQL text executed by sqlite3, enabling injection. [verified: Same unsanitized route-to-format-string-to-executemany chain as [0]; no compensating control.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via urlopen — Server-side requests to internal/metadata services, enabling internal network scanning or cloud credential theft. [verified: Duplicate/overlapping report of the same urlopen sink at ssrf.py:51; still a genuine unguarded SSRF path.]

Server-side request forgery via unvalidated urlopen target — Attacker can force the server to make arbitrary outbound HTTP(S) requests to internal/external hosts, enabling internal network scanning or metadata endpoint access. [verified: Intentionally-vulnerable fixture: urlopen called on unvalidated user_input with no allowlist/scheme check, reachable from Flask routes per threat model's SSRF priority class.]

Server-side request forgery via user-controlled connection host — Attacker-controlled hostname used to open outbound TCP/TLS connections, enabling SSRF against internal services. [verified: HTTPConnection/HTTPSConnection built directly from user-controlled host with no validation, matching the same SSRF sink pattern.]

XML external entity injection via lxml.etree.fromstring on user input — Attacker-supplied XML with external entity declarations can read local files or trigger SSRF/DoS via entity expansion. [verified: lxml.etree.fromstring with default parser (no resolve_entities=False/no_network) resolves external entities on user-controlled input, enabling XXE.]

Reflected XSS in raw WSGI app — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in a victim's browser via crafted query string. [verified: user_input from query string is interpolated directly into HTML output with no escaping on the xss.do_raw path, a reachable reflected XSS sink.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY and DEBUG=True — Predictable SECRET_KEY enables forging signed cookies/tokens; DEBUG=True leaks stack traces, source snippets, and settings on error pages [verified: Same confirmed misconfiguration as [0]; duplicate finding of the same lines.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY and DEBUG=True in application settings — A known/hardcoded SECRET_KEY undermines session/cookie signing and CSRF protections; DEBUG=True can leak stack traces, source code, and settings to attackers in error pages. [verified: apps/django_app.py hardcodes SECRET_KEY='test_key' and DEBUG=True with no environment override, a genuinely present insecure config on the app's reachable settings path.]

Reflected XSS via Jinja2 template rendering of unescaped user_input — Attacker-controlled query parameter rendered into HTML template, enabling script injection if the template does not explicitly escape it. [verified: user_input from request.args flows unescaped into template via `{{ user_input | safe }}` in xss.html, with no sanitization; reflected XSS confirmed.]

Reflected XSS in aiohttp xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim browser via crafted user_input query parameter [verified: user_input query param is concatenated unescaped into text/html response body with no sanitization or auto-escaping, reflecting attacker script directly.]

Reflected XSS in Bottle xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim browser via crafted user_input parameter [verified: Line 39 concatenates unescaped user_input directly into the HTML response with no sanitization or template auto-escaping, reachable via GET/POST at /vulnpy/xss/raw.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped user_input in Django HttpResponse — Attacker-controlled request parameter reflected unescaped in HTML response. [verified: user_input from GET/POST is concatenated unescaped into the HttpResponse body when name=='xss' and trigger=='raw', with no HTML escaping or CSP; this is a reachable route parameter, not a sanitizing control.]

Reflected XSS in Django ASGI xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim's browser via the Django ASGI XSS demo route [verified: user_input from GET/POST is concatenated directly into the HTML string returned via HttpResponse with no escaping, and this is plain string building (not a Django template with autoescape), so a script payload in user_input reflects unescaped into the response.]

Reflected XSS in Falcon (sync) xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim's browser, enabling session theft/credential harvesting [verified: user_input from req.get_param is concatenated unescaped into the HTML response body at line 123 with no sanitization/escaping anywhere in the call path.]

Reflected XSS in Falcon ASGI xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim's browser [verified: user_input from req.get_param is concatenated directly into resp.text with content_type text/html and no escaping, so reflected script executes in the browser; this is an intentional vulnerable test fixture.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped user_input concatenated into HTML response — Attacker-controlled request parameter is reflected unescaped in the HTML response, enabling script injection in the victim's browser. [verified: user_input from request headers/args/form is concatenated raw into HTML response with no escaping, and this is the intended demo vuln path.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped user_input concatenation — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in a victim's browser session (session theft, CSRF-token exfiltration). [verified: Same sink as idx 0: template += "

XSS: " + user_input + "

" with no escaping/sanitization anywhere in the call chain.]

Reflected XSS in Pyramid xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim browser via crafted user_input parameter [verified: user_input from request GET/POST is concatenated unescaped directly into the HTML Response body at line 51 with no sanitization or escaping present in this handler.]

Reflected XSS in Quart xss/raw route — Attacker-controlled script executes in victim browser via crafted user_input header or query parameter [verified: user_input from header/query is concatenated raw into HTML response with no escaping (blueprint.py:53), and this is an intentional vulnerable fixture route by design.]

XPath injection via unsanitized user input in findall/findtext expression — Attacker-controlled XPath expression can alter document traversal logic, potentially exposing data outside the intended query. [verified: user_input is passed unsanitized directly as the XPath/ElementPath expression to findall/findtext (lines 25,29,34) with no validation, allowing injection to alter traversal logic against the in-memory XML tree.]

Jinja2 Environment created without autoescape enabled — Any future template rendered through this Environment lacks HTML auto-escaping by default, widening the XSS attack surface beyond the single documented sink [verified: Environment(loader=loader) at line 11 has no autoescape=True, so raw Jinja2 default (no autoescaping) applies to any template rendered via this Environment, widening XSS surface beyond the single |safe sink.]

Insecure session cookie flags (Secure/HttpOnly disabled) — Session cookies can be intercepted over unencrypted connections and stolen via XSS/JS access, enabling session hijacking [verified: Duplicate of idx 1: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/HTTPONLY explicitly disabled at flask_app.py:29-30.]

Insecure session cookie configuration (missing Secure and HttpOnly flags) — Session cookies can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP and are accessible to client-side JavaScript, increasing risk of session hijacking via network interception or XSS. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY are explicitly set False at lines 29-30, a genuinely absent control on a reachable path.]

Missing authentication on dangerous trigger endpoints — Any unauthenticated network client can invoke command execution, SQL injection, deserialization, and code-execution sinks directly. [verified: add_url_rule registers all trigger routes with no permission_classes/auth decorator of any kind, matching the intentional-vulnerability threat model.]

Use of weak MD5 hash algorithm — MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks; using it for integrity or security purposes can be bypassed by an attacker crafting colliding inputs. [verified: do_hashlib_md5 in hash.py hashes input with MD5 and is exposed as an intentional trigger endpoint, matching the benchmark's weak-crypto vuln class with no compensating control.]

Use of broken cryptographic hash functions (MD5/SHA1) — Enables hash-collision attacks against any integrity/identity check built on these digests [verified: Duplicate of idx 0/1 covering both MD5 and SHA1 usage in the same file; both are genuinely weak hash algorithms used on attacker-influenced input with no mitigation.]

Insecure PRNG (random module) seeded/exposed with attacker input — Predictable pseudo-random output could allow forging of any security token derived from this generator [verified: Same file confirms _seed exposes attacker-controlled seeding of the non-cryptographic random module, making output fully predictable — genuinely absent secure-randomness control.]

Insecure security headers (X-XSS-Protection disabled, permissive caching, zero-age HSTS) — Disabling browser XSS filtering and HSTS, and allowing public caching of sensitive responses, increases exposure to XSS and downgrade/MITM attacks and sensitive data caching by shared caches. [verified: app.py:33 sets Cache-Control: public, X-XSS-Protection: 0, and HSTS max-age=0 unconditionally, a genuinely absent/weakened control on every response.]

Insecure security headers (disabled XSS protection / HSTS / caching) — Weakens client-side defense-in-depth, increasing exploitability of reflected XSS and enabling shared-cache exposure of responses. [verified: Same header misconfiguration as idx 0 (duplicate finding); headers are genuinely insecure on every response.]
